known_gaps: Byte-scan proof is strict: short removed strings (< 6 bytes, e.g. kerned word pieces, subset glyph codes) are excluded from the scan (RedactedOutput.short_needles) because they legitimately occur elsewhere; for natural-language documents a distinctive removed word that also appears elsewhere (kept text) yields hits and is_proven() == false. The structural proof is residual_in_region == 0 on a fresh pass over the saved bytes (same region test, so not independent of the interpreter).

Whole strings are removed (a string straddling the region edge is removed entirely); standard fonts without /Widths use an upper-bound advance, and layout_shift_possible is reported when following text on the line may move.
Rotated pages: region is in default user space (no /Rotate or /CropBox mapping). Encrypted PDFs are structure-only (no decryption).

Same-parser reopen is not independent evidence; the tests use raw byte comparison, an independent miniz_oxide inflate scan of every stream body, and (slice 3) a test-side PDF string extractor as the oracle. Acrobat-saved fixture oracle still pending (Acrobat DC installed, foreground session needs Operator approval per START_LOG D5).

Text inside Type3 glyph procs and tiling patterns and structure ActualText is not edited by redaction; the payload proof flags the removed strings if they survive there (sanitize drops Thumb/PieceInfo/XMP on request). Outline titles and annotation text are covered since slice 3.

is_proven is strict by design: a distinctive removed word that also lives in metadata (Info/XMP) is a hit; with a text policy the same word in outline titles and annotation text is redacted (slice 3). region_cleared gives the per-instance answer.
decisions: Object numbers are preserved on full save (no renumbering) so unmodified objects can be copied byte-verbatim; free numbers get a linked free list.
Redaction rewrites the page content into a NEW object and repoints /Contents instead of editing shared streams in place.
Fail closed on unsupported painted content by default; ReportAndContinue is an explicit caller choice.
Signed documents are refused for every mutation including full save (a full rewrite invalidates byte-range signatures); incremental policy is later scope.

notes.slice3_spec_basis: ISO 32000 outline item dictionary (12.3.3), annotation dictionary Contents/T/Subj/RC (12.5.2, 12.5.6.2), appearance dictionary N/R/D (12.5.5), field dictionary V/DV (12.7.4.1), text strings (7.9.2.2: PDFDocEncoding, UTF-16BE FE FF, UTF-8 EF BB BF). PDFDocEncoding 0x18-0x1F/0x80-0x9E/0xA0 table checked against mozilla/pdf.js src/core/string_utils.js. Table numbers differ between ISO 32000-1 (Table 153 outline item, 164/170 annotation, 168 appearance, 220 field) and -2 (151, 168/170, 226); the ISO text itself could not be fetched (10 MB limit), secondary sources agree.
slice3_decisions: Replacement is always a DIRECT value in the holder dictionary (copy-on-write): a shared string object is never edited; it drops out of the save when no other reference remains, else the proof reports it as a hit.

Defaults fail closed: case-insensitive substring; whole_token (the proof's token rule) and case_insensitive=false are options. The proof stays case-sensitive exact-spelling, so it is never stricter than the redaction.

Field/widget /T is a NAME (12.7.4.1): never rewritten (would break uniqueness), reported KeptByPolicy and remains a proof hit; widget_values is the explicit option for /V /DV and the widget appearance.

Annotation appearance streams hold the rendered text: dropped when their show operands match (viewers regenerate); the proof counts a show-operand match in an /AP stream as a hit instead of a kept-text collision (behaviour change vs slice 2 only for annotations whose appearance repeats a removed word).
An annotation's /AP is also dropped when the annotation was edited and an appearance stream cannot be decoded (cannot show it is free of the text).
Direct annotation dictionaries inside /Annots are edited in place in their holder (page or array object); outcome has direct=true and the holder as object.
AcroForm /NeedAppearances is not set after a widget appearance is dropped (catalog untouched); a viewer that does not regenerate shows an empty widget.
slice3_known_gaps: CLOSED by slice 4 (kept for history): named-destination names, action /URI, field /Opt and /TU, structure-tree /ActualText, popup/IRT annotations outside /Annots, composite-font codes in appearance streams (read through /ToUnicode).
Rich text is judged by three spellings (raw, tags removed, tags as gaps) with the common entities decoded; XHTML in a non-UTF-8 stream without a byte-order mark is read as UTF-8.
The needle is a Unicode string; redact_and_save_with bridges from content-stream bytes by PDFDocEncoding decoding of the distinctive (>= 6 byte) removed strings.

slice4_decisions: Destination names are identifiers: a matching name is renamed to a unique opaque HskRdN (not Replace/Remove text) so links keep working and keys never collide; the tree is rebuilt flat and sorted (valid, unbalanced) instead of patching /Limits.
Reference rewrite covers direct /Dest, /OpenAction and GoTo /D values (name or string); an indirect string reference stays a proof hit. GoToR/Launch targets are not touched.
Info + XMP: every string entry of the trailer /Info (custom keys too) and the catalog /Metadata stream (any match drops the key, like /RC) are one policy class, info_fields, default on.
Structure elements are recognised by /S plus /P (or /Type /StructElem); direct dictionaries without /P are not.
Unverifiable is a new outcome kind: an appearance the redaction cannot read on an UNEDITED annotation is kept and flips report.complete to false; on an EDITED annotation it is dropped.
The payload proof stays a byte scan: text visible only through a /ToUnicode CMap is judged by the redaction scan (appearance_scan), not by verify_payload_absent.
slice4_known_gaps: GoToR/Launch /D and /F targets, other name trees (embedded file names, JavaScript names), page/image /Metadata, field /TM and /MK captions, structure elements that are direct dictionaries without /P: not covered, still proof hits.
ToUnicode: bounded parser (codespacerange, bfchar, bfrange); cidchar/cidrange and usecmap are not interpreted; mixed-length codespaces decode greedily by ascending length.
Per-object outcomes for the name tree report the holder of the tree root, not each leaf (leaves are rebuilt away).
